title: Algebra: Equations, Surds, Indices, Logarithms, Functions
relevance: Campus and OA quant screens use algebra to test fast equation setup, identities, and minimization without calculus.

phases.goal: Establish the core identities for indices, surds, logs, and quadratic roots.

must_hit.point: Index laws: product adds exponents, quotient subtracts, power multiplies exponents; negative exponent is reciprocal; fractional exponent is a root.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States x^a x^b = x^{a+b}, x^a/x^b = x^{a-b}, (x^a)^b = x^{ab}, x^{-a}=1/x^a, and x^{a/b} as a root.

must_hit.point: To rationalise 1/(√a+√b), multiply numerator and denominator by √a−√b.
Log laws: product→sum, quotient→difference, power→coefficient; change of base log_b x = log_c x / log_c b.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recalls all four log identities including change of base.

must_hit.point: For ax²+bx+c=0: roots via quadratic formula; sum α+β=−b/a; product αβ=c/a; discriminant Δ=b²−4ac classifies real distinct, equal, or complex roots.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives formula, Vieta relations, and Δ>0 / =0 / <0 cases.

probes: State the index, surd, logarithm, and quadratic-root formulas you rely on in aptitude algebra.

hints.1: Start from the definition block: indices, surds, logs, then quadratics.
hints.2: List each family as a short identity set, including discriminant sign cases.
hints.3: Include rationalising with conjugate and Vieta sum/product with Δ=b²−4ac.

phases.goal: Show how to set up and solve linear, quadratic, surd/index, log, function, and inequality problems.

must_hit.point: Simultaneous linear systems can be added when the ask is a sum of unknowns (e.g. p+n or x+y) without solving each variable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds 2p+3n=18 and 3p+2n=17 to get 5(p+n)=35 so p+n=7, or adds license equations to get x+y=40.

must_hit.point: Two-digit reverse difference is always 9 times the digit difference; with digit sum 12 and reverse greater by 18, original is 57.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses 9(y−x)=18 with x+y=12 to get digits 5 and 7.

must_hit.point: Equal real roots need Δ=0; for kx²−12x+9=0 that forces k=4.
Compare surds by raising to a common power (LCM of indices); for √2, ∛3, fourth-root of 4, sixth-root of 6, LCM 12 shows ∛3 is largest.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares 64, 81, 64, 36 after twelfth powers and picks ∛3.

must_hit.point: Digit count of a positive integer: if log₁₀ N = characteristic c plus mantissa, digits = c+1; for 6⁵⁰ with given logs, log₁₀ N=38.905 so 39 digits.
AM–GM: for positive a,b, (a+b)/2 ≥ √(ab); minimum of 4x+9/x is 12.

probes: Walk through solving a simultaneous system for a combined cost, a discriminant-equal-roots condition, and an AM–GM minimum of the form ax+b/x.

hints.1: Pick one linear add-trick, one Δ=0 quadratic, and one AM–GM example.
hints.2: For logs digit count, separate characteristic and mantissa; for surds, use a common exponent.
hints.3: Cite p+n=7 or x+y=40, k=4 from Δ=0, and min 4x+9/x=12 via AM–GM.

phases.goal: Choose the faster algebraic path over brute-force solving or calculus.

must_hit.point: Prefer adding/scaling equations when only a linear combination (like x+y or p+n) is needed instead of full elimination for each unknown.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains why adding license or pen/notebook equations is enough for the total.

must_hit.point: Prefer AM–GM over calculus for minimizing ax+b/x forms; the minimum is always 2√(ab).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States OAs use AM–GM for these minima and quotes min=2√(ab).

must_hit.point: Bill shortfall trick: assume all smaller denomination, then shortfall divided by per-bill upgrade yields count of larger bills.
must_hit.evidence_hint: If all 46 bills were fives → 230; shortfall 110 / extra 5 → 22 tens.

probes: When would you add equations or use AM–GM instead of solving every variable or taking a derivative?

hints.1: Think about what the question actually asks for—sum, min, or each unknown.
hints.2: Contrast full solve vs add-for-sum, and calculus vertex vs AM–GM for ax+b/x.
hints.3: Name add-for-(x+y), AM–GM min=2√(ab), and the all-fives shortfall trick.

phases.goal: Map OA-style tech wordings to the same algebraic techniques.

must_hit.point: License mix: 40x+100y=2600 and swap 100x+40y=3000; adding gives total licenses x+y=40.
Quadratic profit P(x)=−2x²+120x−1000 is maximized at x=−b/(2a)=30 with P(30)=800.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses vertex formula and substitutes to get 800.

must_hit.point: Capacity C(n)=27^{n/3}×9^{n/2} reduces to 3^{2n}; needing 3¹⁰ gives n=5.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rewrites both bases as powers of 3, equates 2n=10.

must_hit.point: For f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)−4 with f(2)=10, shift g(x)=f(x)−4 to get Cauchy, then f(x)=3x+4 and f(7)=25.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines g, finds c=3, evaluates f(7)=25.

must_hit.point: Latency T=2C+32/C+5 minimized by AM–GM on 2C+32/C (≥16) plus 5 → T_min=21 ms.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gets variable part ≥16, adds 5 for 21 ms.

probes: Solve an OA-style licensing, profit-max, scaling, functional-equation, or latency-min problem using the algebra above.

hints.1: Strip the story and write the equations or function given.
hints.2: Match technique: add system, vertex, common base, constant shift, or AM–GM.
hints.3: Recover x+y=40, P_max=800, n=5, f(7)=25, or T_min=21 ms.

tradeoffs.topic: Adding equations vs solving each unknown
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When the ask is only a sum like p+n or x+y, add the equations (or a multiple) directly; full elimination wastes time if individual values are not needed.

tradeoffs.topic: AM–GM vs calculus for ax + b/x minima
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For positive terms of form ax+b/x, AM–GM gives the minimum 2√(ab) without derivatives; calculus is unnecessary for these OA patterns.

tradeoffs.topic: Bill shortfall trick vs full variables
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Assume all bills are the smaller denomination, then shortfall divided by the per-bill upgrade equals the count of larger bills—faster than a two-variable system when only one count is asked.

gotchas.trap: Treating log₁₀ N’s integer part as the digit count.
gotchas.correction: If log₁₀ x = c + m with mantissa m≥0, the number of digits is c+1 (e.g. 38.905 → 39 digits).

gotchas.trap: Forgetting that a two-digit number minus its reverse is 9 times the digit difference.
gotchas.correction: Difference is always 9×(difference of digits); use with digit sum to solve quickly.

gotchas.trap: Maximizing/minimizing a quadratic by trial instead of the vertex.
gotchas.correction: Absolute max/min of ax²+bx+c is at x=−b/(2a).

gotchas.trap: Leaving a constant in Cauchy-like functional equations.
gotchas.correction: For f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+k forms, shift (e.g. g(x)=f(x)−4 when k=−4) to reach g(x+y)=g(x)+g(y) and g(x)=cx.

gotchas.trap: Using calculus by default for ax+b/x style minima in OAs.
gotchas.correction: AM–GM applies directly; minimum of ax+b/x is 2√(ab).
